old: Its name once pointed only to a drink brewed from a bean, not the buffet of food you'd find there today.
In Mexican Spanish, the word this comes from simply meant 'coffeehouse.'
It shares a root with cafetière, the French word for a coffee pot.
clues: This kind of place to eat began in Mexican Spanish as a word for a coffeehouse, built from the name for a coffee maker.
A self-service dining room where you carry a tray along a counter and pick your own food, unlike a restaurant with waiters. In English, coffee stopped being the point.
Students line up here at lunchtime with trays. Its French cousin, the cafetière, is a coffee pot descended from the same Arabic root for coffee.
